GUIDE FOR RETRIEVAL AND ANALYSIS METALLIC ORTHOPAEDIC IMPLANTS

OF

1. Scope -This guide covers the protocol for the retrieval and analysis of metallic implants used in human patients. It applies to all implants removed from the patient for of clinical and implant performance evaluation.

orthopaedic the purpose

b

2. Summary of the Guide -This guide covers the clinical data to be recorded and the material characterizations to be performed when an implant is retrieved. The clinical data include a case history review, roentgenogram review, tissue culture, and histological evaluation of tissue. The meterial characterizations include chemical composition, macroscopic and microscopic examination ant mechanical property determinations. A photographic documentation of findings shall be made in accordance with the requirements of this guide. 3. Significance -This is a test protocol for standardizing the retrieval and analysis of orthopaedic metallic implants. The results obtained by several independent investigators using this protocol can be correlated in order to relate the performance with materials characteristics. Performance criteria can be established and information useful for updating material and device standards can be generated. 4. Implant Retrieval implant record in place prior to of the implant and

4.1 Photographic Record - If possible, make a photographic record of the its removal. Also, immediately after its removal, make a photographic surgical site. 4.2 Microbiological Culture Obtain a swab prior to implant removal.

4.3 Tissue Sample - Prior to implant removal or immediately a location adjacent to the implant and, if possible, extending of the site of tissue removal relative to the implant.

thereafter, obtain into normal tissue.

5.1 .I Functional level lower limb implants only. be made and recorded. 5.1.2 Examination

of patient attained between insertion and removalThe criteria are for If the report is for other than a lower limb implant, a similar analysis should

of tissue

5.1.2.1 Record the gross characteristics of the tissue immediately adjacent to the implant as to consistency and colour, as seen by the naked eye, and with a hand lens or dissecting microscope. Process the excised tissue for histopathological and for such other studies as are appropriate; elective histological, chemical, mechanical, radiological, etc. Cut the sample into appropriate fractions for such studies. Use standard laboratory practice for the histological preparation of the tissue with regard to the trimming of tissue blocks, fixation, washing, embedding, and staining. Report the methodology. 5.1.2.2 Histopathological observations - Classify the amount of tissue reaction in regard to the thickness of the scar, the presence of leucocytes or other tissue cells, the presence of particles detectable by polarized light, and such other indications of interaction of tissue and material as might be observed. Note evidence of neoplasia or tissue degeneration. Attach a copy of the histopathological report.

6.2 Fractographic Examination (If Implant is Fractured) - Analyze the fracture surface by suitable techniques to ascert in the mode of fracture. In no event should the fracture surface be destructively evaluated. If the device has mechanically failed, it is important to remember that it may be classified as legal evidence. 6.3 Standard Form - A standard form indicating given in Appendix B.
